decision.question: Should we launch a free plan?
decision.objective: Evaluate financial runway, acquisition velocity, infra strain, and cannibalization of launching a free tier.

findings.claim: Runway is 13.2 months ($1.65M cash). Free plan without strict usage caps risks compressing runway below the 10.0-month safety threshold.

evidence.snippet: Cash balance: $1,650,000.00, Net monthly burn: $125,000.00, Runway: 13.2 months.

limitations: Assumes fixed baseline opex without secondary headcount expansion.

findings.claim: A friction-free entry tier will unlock top-of-funnel velocity, generating 3,800+ signups/mo.

evidence.snippet: Site receives 65,000 unique visitors/month with only 1100 trial starts.

limitations: Dependent on product onboarding self-serve experience.

findings.claim: Infrastructure can absorb up to 5,000 free users if rate limits and database storage quotas are strictly capped.

evidence.snippet: Baseline cloud spend is $14,500/mo; estimated free-user cost is $1.15/user/mo.

limitations: Requires engineering to implement Redis-based quota enforcers.

findings.claim: Starter plan ($79/mo) faces cannibalization risk of 8-15% if the free tier includes exports or integrations.

evidence.snippet: Currently 655 active paying subscribers, with 450 on Starter ($79/mo).

limitations: Survey sample on Starter users is limited to last quarter.

findings.claim: Strategy B (Usage Caps) creates the most natural friction point for self-serve upgrades without gating essential utility.

evidence.snippet: Capping at 3 team members and 500 tickets/mo protects 92% of Starter value proposition.

limitations: Depends on UI upgrade prompts deployed in app.

findings.claim: Challenged 1 assumption(s). Growth's conversion estimate of 3.5% lacks historical self-serve telemetry in NimbusDesk's data and carries external research provenance.

evidence.snippet: Downgraded confidence on 1 speculative assumption(s).

limitations: Skeptic review based strictly on submitted findings and historical data.
